Writer seam: SQLiteEventJournalWriter.appendWithExtension (lines 60-82) owns its IMMEDIATE transaction through db.transaction(...).immediate(); appendPreparedWithExtension (99-138) opens and commits its own transaction too and is not the borrowed seam. The new synchronous borrowed-transaction operation shares one body with appendWithExtension (AppendEventBatchSchema.parse, canonicalizeCommandIdentityV1, duplicate-eventId check, appendInTransaction) and neither begins nor commits. Red test: call it inside a caller-owned db.transaction and assert the batch is absent after the outer rollback and present only after the outer commit; this test must fail on the unmodified baseline.

Store seam: ICampaignEventStore.appendCommandBatch is optional (line 185); JournalCampaignEventStore.appendCommandBatch (line 434) reaches journal.appendWithExtension (line 325). The optional synchronous guard runs inside that transaction before the batch is written; a refusal is a typed result arm, not an Error.name match; a store without the capability fails closed when a guard is supplied (choose typed refusal or throw-before-any-write, state which, and test it in JournalCampaignEventStore.test.ts).

Host plumbing: CampaignMatchHost.commitEvents (551-578) takes the batch path only when eventStore.appendCommandBatch exists and otherwise falls back to commitCampaignEventsInSequence, which has no transaction to guard; with a guard supplied the fallback must fail closed. CampaignCommitOutcome (campaignHostBatchCommit.ts:61, today 'committed' | 'lost-race') gains the typed arms for prewrite refusal, known commit, uncertain commit and post-commit cleanup; resultOfCommit maps each; every outcome.kind consumer is made exhaustive so typecheck proves no arm is dropped. No cross-file atomicity claim in code comments or receipts.

Trust boundary: guard and notification callbacks are server-only operation inputs. Test that canonicalizeCommandIdentityV1's digest for a batch is identical with and without a guard, and that no wire schema in @/types/multiplayer/Protocol gains a field for them.

Production inertness: server.js composes no guard. Record that the default-absent path is behaviour-equivalent: the 35 suites of A1/A2 plus B's two named test leaves pass unchanged, and CampaignMatchHost.pipeline.test.ts carries the real-SQLite released-reservation removal cases the Task 15 amendment requires.
Red-first proof is required (unlike A1/A2): the red receipt must show the new assertions failing on the unmodified baseline with the failure text, not a baseline pass.
